correctness.rationale: For nu>p-1, determinant-power weighting is valid on an open interval around zero and exactly sends W_p(nu,Sigma) to W_p(nu+2s,Sigma). Differentiating the tilted mean gives Cov(W,log det W)=2 Sigma entrywise. Whitening gives Q with chi-square(nu p) Laplace transform, while Bartlett decomposition gives Var(log det W) as the stated trigamma sum. Trigamma asymptotics are uniform for fixed proportional aspect ratio; the p/nu->0 and p/nu->1 endpoint arguments use respectively the same expansion and the lower bound psi_1(x)>1/x. The deterministic joint-transform checker numerically differentiates an independent closed-form transform over a parameter grid and confirms all finite formulas and asymptotic regimes.

originality.rationale: The closest full same-model source, Cai--Liang--Zhou (arXiv:1309.0482), was read through its model, main logdet CLTs, Bartlett lemma, and variance proof; it contains no trace occurrence and no inspected mixed trace/logdet statement. Letac--Massam covers invariant polynomial Wishart moments but not logarithmic mixed moments in its stated scope. Bai--Silverstein is a genuine broader asymptotic coverage risk for the proportional interior limit, but an asymptotic LSS theorem does not subsume the exact finite matrix identity Cov(W,log det W)=2 Sigma. Ten semantic database searches and alias web searches found no exact finite match, and current/prior own ledgers contain no Wishart/logdet finding.
residual_risks: A standard exponential-family or matrix-variate textbook may contain the derivative identity Cov(W,log det W)=2 Sigma without using the search phrasing above.
The proportional interior correlation limit may be obtainable directly as a corollary of Bai--Silverstein or related joint LSS central limit theory.
The individual marginal facts used in the proof are classical; originality is claimed only for the exact mixed covariance formulation and its unified aspect-ratio interpretation.

value.rationale: Trace and determinant are canonical additive and multiplicative summaries of multivariate scatter, and logdet is directly tied to Gaussian entropy and generalized variance. The result identifies their exact finite dependence, not merely their marginal laws. The aspect-ratio law shows a structural transition from near-perfect standardized alignment when dimension is thin relative to degrees of freedom, through an explicit nontrivial proportional limit, to decorrelation at the square hard edge. This is a natural dependence question with direct interpretation in high-dimensional covariance geometry; the contribution is not a parameter renaming or a finite numerical improvement.
